shortDescription: The Baltic Exchange's dry bulk freight index, which tracks rates for ships carrying dry bulk commodities, inched up on Tuesday, buoyed by stronger capesize rates.

children: The Baltic Exchange's dry bulk freight index, which tracks rates for ships carrying dry bulk commodities, inched up on Tuesday, buoyed by stronger capesize rates.
, which tracks rates for capesize, panamax and supramax vessels, rose 9 points, or 0.3%, to 3,584.
The capesize index (.BACI) was up 27 points, or 0.4%, to 6,313.
Average daily earnings for capesize vessels (.BATCA), which typically transport 150,000-ton cargoes, including iron ore and coal, increased by $242 to $53,570.

Iron ore prices rose for a fourth straight session, helped by falling shipments and hopes of demand picking up seasonally in top consumer China, although elevated portside stocks and thin steel margins limited gains.
The panamax index (.BPNI) fell 17 points, or 0.7%, to reach 2,414.
Average daily earnings for panamax vessels (.BPWT), which usually carry 60,000 to 70,000 tons of coal or grain, fell $154 to $21,724.
The supramax index (.BSIS) was up 11 points, or 0.7%, to 1,693.
